summary: Insurance Product Information Document (IPID) for LALUX Assurances' multi-risk home insurance easyPROTECT-Home, for a private and individual home or condominium. The document states that easyPROTECT Home is a multi-risk insurance available in 3 formulas (Security, Comfort, Performance), covering the home and its contents whether it is a house, apartment or condominium and whether the insured is owner, co-owner or tenant, and that civil liability (excluding automobile) of the individuals living in the residence and building civil liability can also be covered. The covered box lists the SECURITY guarantees, the coverages added by COMFORT and by PERFORMANCE, five optional extensions for COMFORT and PERFORMANCE, annual travel insurance, home assistance and the easyPROTECT Discover component. All three lists carry the printed note "Non-exhaustive list".

gaps: REVERSED READING ORDER on page 1, rebuilt from coordinates. The text layer emits the header (y 27-97), then the covered box left column (x0 29.8 / 43.9, y 313-753), then the right column (x0 307.6 / 321.7, y 275-800) which carries the tail of the covered box, the whole "What is not covered  ?" box and the whole "Are there exclusions from coverage ?" box - and ONLY THEN the two full-width blocks "Disclaimer:" (x0 31.2, y 130-157) and "What type of insurance is this ?" (x0 22.7, y 180-225), which are printed at the TOP of the page above both columns. Read flat, the definition of the product lands after the last exclusion. Attachment was rebuilt by abscissa and ordinate, not by proximity in the flow.

The "What is covered ?" box SPANS BOTH COLUMNS: it starts in the left column with SECURITY and ends in the right column with "Annual travel insurance", "Home assistance" and "easyPROTECT Discover" (x0 307.6, y 275.8-398.9), above the "What is not covered  ?" heading at y 440.6. Those three guarantees are therefore COVERED items, not exclusions, even though they sit in the same column as the two exclusion boxes. This is the one place in this document where a flat read could invert polarity, and it was resolved by coordinates and by the bullet images (below).

Polarity verified from the bullet images, which are placed IMAGES - not text and not vector drawings. Page 1 carries 39 images in three sizes, one per box, and the arithmetic closes exactly: 26 x 120x133 px (green tick) for the 26 ticked items of "What is covered ?"; 8 x 120x121 px (red cross) for the 8 items of "What is not covered  ?"; 5 x 40x148 px (orange exclamation mark) for the 5 items of "Are there exclusions from coverage ?". 26 + 8 + 5 = 39. The 26 green ticks break down as 7 SECURITY + 3 COMFORT + 6 PERFORMANCE + 5 optional extensions + 1 annual travel + 1 home assistance + 3 easyPROTECT Discover. Confirmed on 6x renders. Page 2 carries no images at all. This count is not a text observation and therefore appears in no key_quote.

RUBRIC DEFECT, preserved and NOT repaired: the third box is titled "Are there exclusions from coverage ?" and carries the orange exclamation-mark icon that the EU IPID template uses for its RESTRICTIONS box. Unlike the restrictions box of the template, its five entries are genuine exclusions (willful disregard of laws, neglect of maintenance, crime or intentional offense, war, nuclear) and not restrictions, so here the printed title agrees with the content while the template slot does not. The consequence for a reader is that this document contains NO restrictions section at all: no deductible, no ceiling, no proportional rule anywhere on the two pages.

is_optional is genuinely ambiguous for the six PERFORMANCE coverages and is recorded as true with the reason spelled out in `conditions`. The document prints them under "PERFORMANCE = CONFORT + the following coverages:" - so they are INCLUDED by default in the PERFORMANCE formula - while each item is individually annotated "(optional for COMFORT)" - so the same coverage is an optional add-on in the COMFORT formula. One boolean cannot carry both readings; true was chosen because the document itself uses the word "optional", and the formula-by-formula wording is reproduced verbatim in each coverage's `conditions`.

is_optional is null for "Annual travel insurance", "Home assistance" and "easyPROTECT Discover". They are printed inside the "What is covered ?" box with a green tick, but the document does not say which of the three formulas includes them nor whether they are optional. Null records that absence; it was NOT inferred from their position in the box, and an unticked formula was never read as an exclusion.

Printed typographic and spelling defects, preserved verbatim and NOT corrected: "PERFORMANCE = CONFORT + the following coverages:" - CONFORT is spelled the French way in an English document, while the same formula is spelled COMFORT in the line above and in "(optional for COMFORT)"; "Rainwater entering through openings, wether they are closed or open" - "wether" for "whether", verified on a 6x render, the page really prints it that way; "Theft and breakage of valuable items jewelry, watches, fashion accessories" - no punctuation between "items" and "jewelry"; "(Private and individual home, condominium )" - space before the closing parenthesis; "What is not covered  ?" - double space; "Storm, hail, tornado, and earthquake  " - two trailing spaces.

The product name is printed two ways: "easyPROTECT-Home" with a hyphen in the header line "LALUX Assurances - Product : easyPROTECT-Home", and "easyPROTECT Home" without a hyphen in the body sentence "easyPROTECT Home is a multi-risk insurance...". `product_name` records the hyphenated header form. The formula names are likewise printed in two cases: SECURITY / COMFORT / PERFORMANCE in capitals in the covered box, and "(Security, Comfort, Performance)" in title case in the body sentence. Both readings are recorded; neither was normalised.

"easyPROTECT Discover" is a distinct component listed inside this document, and the document itself says a separate and more comprehensive information document is available for it. It is recorded as a coverage of this product with its three ticked items, NOT as a separate product, and this document was NOT marked as an extension of it. Its own sub-option "Optional: IT mobile coverage." is recorded in the coverage's `conditions`.

No edition date, no version number and no document reference is printed anywhere on the two pages, so `edition_date` and `reference` are null. Two non-printed sources suggest 2023 and were deliberately NOT used: the source URL file name contains "_2023_EN.pdf", and the PDF file metadata gives a creation date of 2023-09-15 09:03:09+02:00, a modification date of 2023-09-15 09:17:33+02:00 and the InDesign source name "IPID_Assurance Habitation_LALUX_easyPROTECT-Habitation_EN.indd". A file name and file metadata are not printed content.

Risk carrier: the document prints only the brand "LALUX Assurances" in its header banner and refers everywhere else to "the company" / "the insurance company". It states no legal form, no RCS number and no address, so it is NOT possible from this document to tell which of the authorised entities underwrites the risk. `insurer_name` records the printed brand "LALUX Assurances" rather than the task metadata value "lalux"; no risk carrier was inferred.

Branch: the task value `habitation` is copied through and is supported by the document ("Multi-risk home insurance", covering the home and its contents). "easyPROTECT" is a commercial range prefix used by LALUX across several branches and was NOT read as a branch. Note that the product as described also carries covers that belong to other branches - civil liability excluding automobile, legal protection, annual travel insurance, home assistance - all of them inside the same home policy; they are recorded as coverages of this product rather than split out.

target_audience is null: the document names no market segment (particuliers / entreprises / independants / secteur public). It describes only the insured's relation to the dwelling ("whether you are an owner, co-owner, or tenant") and, for the Discover component, an age band of 15-27 for people preparing their entry into professional life. That wording is in `target_audience_note`; it was not converted into an audience.

No sums insured, no sub-limits, no deductibles and no waiting periods appear anywhere in this document: `deductibles` and `prescription_period` are null and `waiting_periods` is empty because the document is silent, not because they were skipped. The only figures printed on the two pages are: 1,500 EUR (the threshold above which valuable items fall under the optional extension), 25 km/h (maximum speed of the soft mobility devices), 45 consecutive days (theft during vacancy), the 15-27 age band, eight days (claim declaration), 30 days / one month / 60 days (cancellation) and 24/7 (assistance). Note that 1,500 EUR is printed with an English thousands comma and is recorded exactly as printed.

All three lists carry the printed note "Non-exhaustive list", so the 22 coverages and 13 exclusions recorded are everything the document prints but are expressly not everything that applies to the product. The document refers to general and/or special conditions that it does not reproduce and for which it gives no reference, edition or URL.
